title: The Patient Prathap Reddy Could Not Send Abroad
conflicts: Customs duty on equipment: 375% (Reddy, HBS 2014), 300% (Fortune India 2024), 100% (Reddy to Business Today 2024); story says only 'taxed as a luxury'. Delhi trips: weekly Thursday-to-Sunday (Reddy) versus 'almost 60 trips' (Fortune India); Reddy's description used. Bank finance: half state-bank, half foreign-exchange loan (HBS summary) versus six banks at Rs 5 crore each (Fortune India); story says only 'borrow as a special case'. Land clearance 18 months or two years (both Reddy); both given. The historian Sarah Hodges (IJME 2013) argues the standard founding story overstates Reddy's role and Apollo's effect, and notes the hospital admitted patients only from February 1984; her view is reported in her name.
notes: Slate said a patient 'died waiting to go abroad'; Reddy's own account is that the man could not raise $50,000 for surgery in the US. Main source is the 2014 Harvard Business School oral history (landing page cited; the full transcript is linked from it through an expiring signed URL). The quote stance is 'complicates', applying Analects XV.27 to how the founding legend is received.
